scope.detail: Three of the five declared paths are changed; `apps/api/src/smart-form-validation.ts` and its test are deliberately NOT touched — the validator's participant-relationship check is correct and the defect was that the repository handed it a null teamId. Plus this lane's own artifacts: the manifest, the .ops/sync file and this proof bundle. `packages/db/src/runtime-repositories.ts` is a Tier C EXACT path, which is why this lane is T1 rather than the T3 an earlier draft proposed. No workflow, no merge control, no containment setting, no migration and no deploy path is touched.

limits: This lane changes where `getEventBrowse` and `searchBrowse` READ a player's team identity from — the provider `participants` observation edge instead of the empty canonical `teams` / `player_team_assignments` tables — and not what any published interface promises. No caller signature changes and no client change was required.

It seeds nothing and it deletes nothing. The canonical tables remain empty under parked provider ingestion, deliberately, and every production `participants` row is preserved. The proof-fixture repair is a read filter, never a DELETE; production data deletion is reserved decision 1 and is not proposed.

The fixture-exclusion predicate is the MARKER (`metadata.proofIssue` non-null), never 'has no team relationship'. In today's production data those two predicates select the same 26 rows, so the distinction is invisible in live data and is asserted against constructed rows instead — including a legitimate team-less player that is retained, and a `proofIssue` of JSON null that is retained.

The exclusion was applied only to `getEventBrowse` and `searchBrowse`. `handleSearchPlayers` / `handleSearchTeams` intersect UTV2-1854's already-filtered repository results with the event's participants, so an existing control already guarantees it there; that control is proven rather than duplicated.

`getEventBrowse` also reports `leagueId: null` from the same empty canonical maps. That is real and recorded, and it is NOT a submission blocker — `submission-service.ts` and `smart-form-validation.ts` never read it. It is out of scope here.

The staging receipt proves browse resolution, fixture exclusion, persistence of both pick shapes and non-delivery on a real database. It does not constitute the Milestone 1 pilot, which requires Griff's own browser against the deployed system.
